directions.issue: Title/question target youth, while population is all local adult jobseekers. The sampling population can therefore fail to answer the stated question.
directions.requiredRevision: Define a declared adult-youth age band and local residence/work/intent scope consistently in title, question and population, or broaden the title/question to adult jobseekers. Do not invent current access.
directions.methodNote: If an effect of information format is later claimed, use an appropriate comparison/intervention; an understanding task or consultation intention alone is not observed job-seeking behavior.

directions.assessment: User/non-user comparison is a proposed design rather than a reported difference. Existing minimum evidence correctly begins with verifying current stations and recruiting by actual use history.
Training preferences are a tentative decision problem, not a claim of an existing shortage. Retain actual role stratification, current training-condition checks and permission/confidentiality limits.
unresolved: Whether an identified organization can act on results

directions.assessment: A bounded product-use procurement study is a plausible proposal; the minimum evidence already requires verified products and real purchasing histories. No unmet market need is stated as fact.

directions.issue: Title/question concern local youth, but population is any volunteering adult jobseeker, with no youth or local criterion.
directions.requiredRevision: Specify a declared adult-youth age band and local geographic eligibility, or revise the title/question. Verify actual roles/open positions before showing role materials; the cluster list does not establish vacancies.

directions.assessment: The proposal stays at Chazhuang village and asks rather than asserts first/repeat visitor differences. Its current-opening/transport check and actual-visit recruitment condition are appropriate.
unresolved: Current village access, transport and operator permission
